subject: Clarify: 'Special damages' scope in MSA/Order Form — ACME redlines
summary: External counsel submitted MSA/Order Form redlines focusing on consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages language. Internal team discussed mutual vs one-way exclusion, definition fights, and cap interplay; proposed compromise language and requested sign-off on final redline for DocuSign.
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@acmebio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Garcia <t.garcia@acmebio.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME redlines — MSA (liability / special damages)

Marcus / Laura —

Please find attached ACME's consolidated redlines to the MSA and Order Form (see ACME_MSA_redlines.docx). Our primary asks on liability are:

- A one-way exclusion of consequential, incidental, special and punitive damages in favor of ACME (redline calls this out at §13.2).
- Narrow definition of "consequential" to exclude foreseeable lost profits and business interruption, but ACME must retain recovery for indirect regulatory fines and third-party claims tied to Redwood's service.
- Carve-outs for (i) willful misconduct/gross negligence, (ii) indemnified third-party IP claims, and (iii) data security breaches that lead to regulatory penalties.

Client prefers one-way language because they see Redwood as the service provider carrying operational risk. If Redwood insists on mutual language, ACME would expect either (a) a higher cap on liability in the Order Form or (b) explicit carve-outs for regulatory fines.

Can you review and let us know Redwood's position on mutual vs one-way exclusions and whether you can accept ACME's suggested definition of "consequential damages"?

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Wu
Senior Counsel, ACME Bio
elaine.wu@acmebio.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: ACME_MSA_redlines.docx (redline, 62KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@acmebio.com>, Tom Garcia <t.garcia@acmebio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME redlines — MSA (liability / special damages)

Elaine — thanks for sending. I looped in our legal and contracts leads (Laura and Rishi) to weigh in on the redline specifics. Quick operational ask: can we get a short call early next week to walk through the client's preference on one-way vs mutual exclusions? I'd like to understand the business drivers so we can propose a pragmatic compromise (and avoid a long back-and-forth redline exchange).

Two quick clarifying questions for ACME:
- When ACME references "regulatory fines" as an exception to the exclusion, do you mean direct statutory penalties assessed against ACME (e.g., GDPR fines) or consequential losses to ACME's customers arising from a data incident?
- For the cap interplay: is ACME expecting the Order Form cap to sit above the MSA cap (i.e., per-Order Form fee-based cap) if we move to mutual exclusion?

Happy to propose times — I have availability Mon/Tue morning PT.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@acmebio.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: ACME redlines — MSA (liability / special damages)

Elaine / Marcus —

Thanks for the redline. A few substantive points from our side (high level + proposed language) that we think will get us to a middle ground:

1) Mutual vs one-way exclusion
We prefer mutual exclusions for commercial predictability. One-way exclusions expose Redwood to open-ended downstream liabilities and are inconsistent with our standard commercial program. That said, we're open to limited carve-outs that address ACME's concerns.

Proposed compromise (suggested redline paragraph):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or indirect damages, except to the extent such damages arise from (a) willful misconduct or gross negligence, (b) a party's breach of confidentiality obligations, or (c) third-party claims for intellectual property infringement where the indemnifying party is responsible."

2) Definition fight — "Consequential damages"
ACME's proposed definition is broad. We propose a clearer definition tied to foreseeable categories:
'"Consequential damages' means indirect losses such as lost profits, loss of business, loss of data value, and business interruption that do not flow directly and immediately from the breach itself.'

3) Regulatory fines carve-out
We can carve in regulatory fines only where they arise from the provider's willful misconduct or gross negligence or a material breach of Redwood's documented security obligations. We cannot accept an unlimited exposure where ACME's own misconfiguration or customer obligations are the proximate cause.

4) Cap interplay
If ACME insists on a one-way exclusion in its favor, we would need either (i) to increase the liability cap to a multiple of Order Form fees (e.g., 12 months fees x 2), or (ii) to preserve mutuality but add specific carve-outs (as above).

Please confirm ACME's tolerance for the mutually excluded language above or provide suggested edits. Happy to jump on a call — Marcus, I can do Mon 9:30 PT.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@acmebio.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Garcia <t.garcia@acmebio.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME redlines — MSA (liability / special damages)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear note. ACME's internal product and legal teams are united behind a one-way exclusion in ACME's favor. The reasoning: ACME will be placing regulated data into Redwood's environment and the pricing model is structured assuming Redwood accepts the operational risk.

That said, ACME is prepared to accept mutual language only if Redwood accepts two commercial concessions:
1) Increase the Order Form liability cap to 24 months of fees for the impacted environment; and
2) Add an explicit carve-out for regulatory fines tied directly to Redwood's proven security failure (i.e., not configuration errors).

If Redwood will not accept either concession, ACME will need the one-way exclusion.

On the narrow definition point, ACME will accept Redwood's proposed definition of consequential damages if the regulatory fines carve-out stays intact.

We can take Laura's language and mark it as "ACME exception" inline. We prefer to resolve this before signature — client would like certainty on the cap/coverage prior to committing to the Dedicated capacity order.

Best,
Elaine

> On Thu, Nov 26, 2026 at 10:20 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Laura's proposed compromise below — we accept the mutual exclusion with carve-outs...

Attachment: OrderForm_ACME_redline.pdf (excerpted liability sections)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@acmebio.com>, Tom Garcia <t.garcia@acmebio.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed compromise language — consequential / special damages (final redline)

Elaine / Tom —

Thanks for the clarity and for flagging ACME's commercial requirement tied to Dedicated capacity. After internal review and a quick business alignment with Marcus, we can offer the following compromise for inclusion in the MSA (and mirrored in the Order Form):

1) Mutual exclusion (final language):
"Except for the types of damages expressly excluded in this section, neither Party shall be liable to the other for incidental, consequential, special, exemplary, punitive or indirect damages, including but not limited to lost profits, loss of business, loss of use, loss of data value, or loss of goodwill, even if such party was advised of the possibility of such damages. The foregoing shall not limit either Party's liability for: (a) willful misconduct or gross negligence; (b) a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations; (c) indemnification obligations arising from third-party intellectual property infringement claims; or (d) regulatory fines or penalties to the extent they are finally adjudicated and caused by the Provider's demonstrable breach of its documented security obligations."

2) Definition: we adopt the Redwood-proposed definition of "Consequential damages" above to reduce ambiguity.

3) Cap interplay / Order Form concession: in recognition of ACME's concerns, Redwood will accept a 12-month fee cap for the specific Dedicated environment tied to this Order Form (i.e., Order Form cap = total recurring fees for 12 months). We cannot accept 24 months at this time. Alternatively, ACME may purchase an uplifted SLA/commercial protection add-on (pricing to be provided) in exchange for a higher cap.

4) Regulatory fines carve-out: we will accept a carve-out for regulatory fines where (i) Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence is the proximate cause; or (ii) there is a final regulatory determination against Redwood. We will not accept exposure for fines where ACME's actions or its customers' acts are the predominant cause.

Next steps: I've attached a tracked redline (Proposed_Liability_Compromise_redline.docx). Please review and advise whether ACME can accept mutual exclusion with the 12-month Order Form cap or whether you need to pursue the 24-month cap. If ACME needs the 24-month cap, Marcus indicated the business can escalate for a commercial concession, but that will take additional approvals.

If we can land on language, Marcus can pull legal sign-off and route for DocuSign.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
Rishi.Malhotra@redwood.com
